notes: Schema is the unit of mastery (BrainLift SPOV1). The flaw axis is PRIMARY (SPOV2). exam_weight values are RELATIVE frequency estimates within each axis (normalized to sum ~1.0 per axis) synthesized from prep-taxonomy sources; they are estimates to be refined with real form-frequency data, and are consumed as schema_weight by the schema-weighted queue. See methodology.md.

LR.name: Logical Reasoning
LR.notes: ~2/3 of scored questions; the primary target.

flaw.description: The reasoning error in an argument. Highest-transfer schema: the same flaw recurs across many question types, so it is the primary organizing and diagnostic axis.

question_type.description: The task the stem announces (surface axis). Useful for labeling and section modeling, secondary to flaw.

trap.description: Wrong-answer (distractor) types. Systematic, so 'why is this wrong' is itself a learnable schema; a student's habitual trap is highly diagnostic (BrainLift Insight 8).

rc_structure.description: Recurring structural targets in Reading Comprehension passages and question stems.

schemas.name: Correlation treated as causation
schemas.description: Concludes X causes Y from mere correlation between X and Y.

schemas.name: Reversed causation
schemas.description: Concludes X causes Y when Y may cause X.

schemas.name: Overlooked common cause
schemas.description: Ignores a third factor Z that causes both X and Y.

schemas.name: Post hoc (temporal-to-causal)
schemas.description: Infers causation from mere temporal sequence (after this, therefore because of this).

schemas.name: Necessary/sufficient confusion
schemas.description: Treats a necessary condition as sufficient or vice versa.

schemas.name: Mistaken reversal
schemas.description: Affirms the consequent: from A->B concludes B->A.

schemas.name: Mistaken negation
schemas.description: Denies the antecedent: from A->B concludes not-A -> not-B.

schemas.name: Unwarranted assumption / term shift
schemas.description: Conclusion introduces a term or scope not established by the premises (a gap).

schemas.name: Unrepresentative / biased / small sample
schemas.description: Generalizes from a sample that is biased, too small, or not representative.

schemas.name: Appeal to ignorance
schemas.description: Treats absence of evidence as evidence of absence (or vice versa).

schemas.name: Part-to-whole / whole-to-part
schemas.description: Assumes what is true of the parts is true of the whole, or vice versa (composition/division).

schemas.name: Percentage vs. absolute number
schemas.description: Confuses a change in proportion with a change in absolute quantity.

schemas.name: Equivocation
schemas.description: Uses one word in two different senses across the argument.

schemas.name: Circular reasoning
schemas.description: Assumes the conclusion among the premises.

schemas.name: Ad hominem
schemas.description: Attacks the source rather than the argument.

schemas.name: Straw man
schemas.description: Misrepresents an opposing view to refute it more easily.

schemas.name: False dilemma
schemas.description: Presents only two options when others exist.

schemas.name: Appeal to authority/emotion
schemas.description: Relies on an illegitimate authority or on emotion instead of evidence.

schemas.name: Faulty comparison / analogy
schemas.description: Compares two things that are not relevantly alike.

schemas.name: Internal contradiction
schemas.description: Premises or conclusion conflict with one another.

schemas.name: Necessary Assumption
schemas.description: Find an assumption the argument requires to be true.

schemas.name: Sufficient Assumption
schemas.description: Find an assumption that, if added, guarantees the conclusion.

schemas.name: Identify the Flaw
schemas.description: Describe the reasoning error in the argument.

schemas.name: Strengthen
schemas.description: Choose the answer that most supports the argument.

schemas.name: Weaken
schemas.description: Choose the answer that most undermines the argument.

schemas.name: Must Be True / Inference
schemas.description: What must be true given the statements.

schemas.name: Most Strongly Supported
schemas.description: What is best supported (not necessarily entailed) by the statements.

schemas.name: Paradox / Resolve-Explain
schemas.description: Resolve an apparent discrepancy between two facts.

schemas.name: Principle (Identify)
schemas.description: Identify the general principle underlying the argument.

schemas.name: Principle (Apply)
schemas.description: Apply a stated principle to a case.

schemas.name: Method of Reasoning
schemas.description: Describe how the argument proceeds.

schemas.name: Parallel Reasoning
schemas.description: Find the argument with matching logical structure.

schemas.name: Parallel Flaw
schemas.description: Find the argument whose flaw matches the stimulus flaw.

schemas.name: Main Conclusion
schemas.description: Identify the main conclusion of the argument.

schemas.name: Role of a Statement
schemas.description: Identify the function a claim plays in the argument.

schemas.name: Point at Issue / Agreement
schemas.description: Identify what two speakers disagree (or agree) about.

schemas.name: Evaluate the Argument
schemas.description: Find the question most relevant to evaluating the argument.

schemas.name: Out of scope
schemas.description: Introduces a consideration irrelevant to the argument's scope.

schemas.name: Too strong / extreme
schemas.description: Overstated language the stimulus does not support.

schemas.name: Too weak
schemas.description: So hedged it fails to do the required job (e.g., for a sufficient assumption).

schemas.name: Opposite
schemas.description: Does the reverse of what the task asks (e.g., weakens on a strengthen).

schemas.name: Reversed relationship
schemas.description: Swaps the direction of a conditional or causal relationship.

schemas.name: Half right / half wrong
schemas.description: One clause is correct, another is not; the whole is wrong.

schemas.name: Premise restatement
schemas.description: Repeats a premise instead of doing the required work.

schemas.name: Could be true (fails must-be-true)
schemas.description: Consistent with the stimulus but not required by it.

schemas.name: Real-world plausible but unsupported
schemas.description: True in the world but not supported by the stimulus.

schemas.name: Right answer to the wrong question
schemas.description: A good answer to a different task than the stem asks.

schemas.name: RC: distortion of author's view
schemas.description: Misstates the author's position or degree of commitment.

schemas.name: RC: wrong-viewpoint attribution
schemas.description: Attributes a view to the wrong party in the passage.

schemas.name: RC: tone mismatch
schemas.description: Answer's tone conflicts with the author's tone.

schemas.name: Main point / primary purpose
schemas.description: The central claim or purpose of the passage.

schemas.name: Author attitude / tone
schemas.description: The author's stance toward the subject or a view.

schemas.name: Passage organization
schemas.description: How the passage is structured.

schemas.name: Viewpoint attribution
schemas.description: Which party holds which view.

schemas.name: Function of a detail
schemas.description: Why the author includes a specific detail.

schemas.name: RC inference
schemas.description: What the passage implies or supports.

schemas.name: Comparative-passage relationship
schemas.description: How two paired passages relate to each other.
